subproblem.title: Bochner integrals over an injective continuous image from a weighted set identity (supplied steps 5–6)
subproblem.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, J : ℝ^m → ℝ measurable and A ⊆ ℝ^m measurable (ℝ^d = Euclid d). Assume G is continuous on A and injective on A, J(w) ≥ 0 for w ∈ A, and μ(G(B)) = ∫_B J dL^m for every measurable B ⊆ A, where the right side is the lower Lebesgue integral of ENNReal.ofReal∘J with respect to L^m = volume. Then for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ (no measurability or integrability assumed), ∫_{G(A)} f dμ = ∫_A J(w)·f(G(w)) dw. Both sides are Bochner integrals, so a non-integrable function has integral 0.

subproblem.natural_proof:

Notation. L^m = volume on ℝ^m. ρ := L^m with density ofReal∘J (volume.withDensity). A carries the subspace topology and σ-algebra, and ν := comap of ρ under the inclusion A → ℝ^m.

1. (Measurable embedding.) Let φ : A → ℝ^P, φ(x) := G(x). φ is continuous because G is continuous on A (ContinuousOn.domRestrict), hence measurable; it is injective because G is injective on A. Let s ⊆ A be measurable in the subtype. Its image in ℝ^m is measurable (MeasurableSet.subtype_image, A measurable), and G is continuous and injective on it. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; ℝ^m is Polish), φ(s) = G(s) is Borel. Hence φ is a measurable embedding.

2. (Identification of μ⌞G(A).) Claim: μ⌞G(A) = φ_#ν. Let Y ⊆ ℝ^P be measurable. Then (μ⌞G(A))(Y) = μ(Y ∩ G(A)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Put A_Y := A ∩ G^{−1}(Y). It is the image in ℝ^m of the measurable set φ^{−1}(Y) of the subtype, hence a measurable subset of A, and Y ∩ G(A) = φ(φ^{−1}(Y)) = G(A_Y). By hypothesis, μ(G(A_Y)) = ∫_{A_Y} J dL^m = ρ(A_Y). On the other side, (φ_#ν)(Y) = ν(φ^{−1}(Y)) = ρ(A_Y), by Measure.map_apply, by MeasurableEmbedding.comap_apply for the inclusion of the measurable set A (MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe), and by withDensity_apply. The two measures agree on measurable sets, so they are equal (Measure.ext).

3. (Change of variables along φ and the inclusion.) Since φ is a measurable embedding, ∫ f d(φ_#ν) = ∫_A f(φ(x)) dν(x) for every f, measurable or not (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). The inclusion A → ℝ^m is also a measurable embedding, and pushing ν forward by it gives ρ⌞A (map_comap_subtype_coe). Hence ∫_A f(φ(x)) dν(x) = ∫ f(G(w)) d(ρ⌞A)(w). Moreover ρ⌞A = (L^m⌞A) with density ofReal∘J (restrict_withDensity).

4. (Removing the density.) Since ofReal(J(w)) = ↑(J(w)⁺) with J⁺ := Real.toNNReal∘J measurable, integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul gives ∫ F d((L^m⌞A) with density ofReal∘J) = ∫_A J(w)⁺·F(w) dw for every F : ℝ^m → ℝ. Take F := f∘G. Since J ≥ 0 on A, J(w)⁺ = J(w) for w ∈ A, so the integrand equals J(w)·f(G(w)) on the measurable set A (setIntegral_congr_fun).

 ∫_{G(A)} f dμ = ∫ f d(μ⌞G(A)) = ∫ f d(φ_#ν) = ∫_A J(w)·f(G(w)) dw.
Every step is an identity of Bochner integrals valid for arbitrary f. In particular, if one side is not integrable, both sides are 0. ∎

subproblem.title: Linear area formula with positive Gram determinant (Simon Ch. 2, 3.1)
subproblem.statement: Let n, P ∈ ℕ and let L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be an injective continuous linear map (ℝ^d = Euclid d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) with Hilbert adjoint L*. Then (i) det(L*∘L) > 0, where det is the determinant of the endomorphism L*∘L of ℝ^n (ContinuousLinearMap.det); and (ii) for every set S ⊆ ℝ^n (no measurability assumed), H^n(L(S)) = √det(L*∘L) · L^n(S) in [0, ∞], where H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, L^n = volume on ℝ^n, and the factor is ENNReal.ofReal √det(L*∘L).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n P : ℕ) (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P), Function.Injective L → 0 < (L.adjoint ∘L L).det ∧ ∀ S : Set (Euclid n), μHE[n] (L '' S) = ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt ((L.adjoint ∘L L).det)) * volume S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 3.1 and the printed argument before it (chapter-02.txt lines 743–759). Simon chooses an orthogonal q of ℝ^{n+k} with q(range ℓ) = ℝ^n × {0} and p(x, y) = x, so that p∘q∘ℓ : ℝ^n → ℝ^n, (p∘q∘ℓ)*(p∘q∘ℓ) = ℓ*ℓ and H^n(q(B)) = H^n(B). Below, κ is the isometry of ℝ^n onto range L (κ* plays the role of p∘q on range L) and M := κ*∘L plays the role of p∘q∘ℓ. This is also step 2 of the supplied proof of the parent node. Mathlib's LinearMap.hausdorffMeasure_image (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/NormDet.lean) uses the same argument but is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.

Notation. ℝ^d = Euclid d; |·| is the Euclidean norm; T* is the Hilbert adjoint (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint); det is the determinant of an endomorphism; H^n = μHE[n]; L^n = volume.

1. (An isometry onto the range.) Let V := range L ⊆ ℝ^P. Since L is injective, dim V = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). Fix an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_n of V (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed by Fin n along dim V = n). Let κ : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, κ(x) := Σ_i x_i τ_i. This is the inclusion V ⊆ ℝ^P composed with the inverse of the coordinate isometry of the basis, so κ is a linear isometry with range κ = V. For every h ∈ ℝ^n, Lh ∈ V, so Lh = κ(u_h), where u_h ∈ ℝ^n is the coordinate vector of Lh in the basis τ.

2. (Factorization L = κ∘M.) Since κ is a linear isometry, κ*∘κ = id_{ℝ^n} (LinearIsometry.adjoint_comp_self). Put M := κ*∘L : ℝ^n → ℝ^n. For h ∈ ℝ^n, κ(Mh) = κ(κ*(κ u_h)) = κ(u_h) = Lh, so κ∘M = L. If Mx = My, then Lx = κMx = κMy = Ly, hence x = y. Thus M is injective, ker M = 0, and det M ≠ 0 (LinearMap.det_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot).

3. (Gram determinant.) By ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp, L*∘L = (κ∘M)*∘(κ∘M) = M*∘(κ*∘κ)∘M = M*∘M. In the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^n, the matrix of M* is the conjugate transpose of the matrix of M (LinearMap.toMatrix_adjoint). Over ℝ this is the transpose, so det M* = det M (LinearMap.det_toMatrix, Matrix.det_conjTranspose). By multiplicativity of det (LinearMap.det_comp), det(L*∘L) = det(M*)·det(M) = (det M)². Since det M ≠ 0, det(L*∘L) > 0, which is (i). Moreover √det(L*∘L) = √((det M)²) = |det M| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).

4. (Measure of the image.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^n be arbitrary. By step 2, L(S) = κ(M(S)). Since κ is an isometry, H^n(κ(X)) = H^n(X) for every X ⊆ ℝ^n, where H^n on the right is μHE[n] of ℝ^n (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image applied to LinearIsometry.isometry). On ℝ^n, μHE[n] = L^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). For the linear endomorphism M of ℝ^n, L^n(M(S)) = |det M|·L^n(S) for every S, with no measurability needed (Measure.addHaar_image_continuousLinearMap). Hence
 H^n(L(S)) = H^n(κ(M(S))) = L^n(M(S)) = |det M|·L^n(S) = √det(L*∘L)·L^n(S),
using |det M| = √det(L*∘L) from step 3 (as ENNReal.ofReal factors). This is (ii).

For n = 0 every step remains valid: ℝ^0 is a point and all the determinants equal 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Since L is injective, range L has dimension n; an orthonormal basis of range L gives a linear isometry κ : ℝ^n → ℝ^P with range κ = range L.
M := κ*∘L satisfies κ∘M = L because κ*κ = id, so M is injective and det M ≠ 0.
L*L = M*κ*κM = M*M and det M* = det M (matrix of the adjoint is the transpose), so det(L*L) = (det M)² > 0 and √det(L*L) = |det M|.
H^n(L S) = H^n(κ(M S)) = L^n(M S) = |det M|·L^n(S) by isometry invariance of μHE[n], μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n and Measure.addHaar_image_continuousLinearMap.

The range isometry gives L = κM; injectivity makes det M nonzero, and det(L*L) = (det M)^2. Isometry invariance and Haar scaling then prove the measure identity without measurability assumptions. The proof also covers dimension zero and has no child or parent reliance.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure of an image under a map bi-Lipschitz relative to a reference map (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i))
subproblem.statement: Let n, P ∈ ℕ, let F, L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be arbitrary maps (ℝ^d = Euclid d), let S ⊆ ℝ^n be an arbitrary set and let a, b ∈ ℝ with a > 0 and b ≥ 0. Suppose a·|L(x) − L(y)| ≤ |F(x) − F(y)| ≤ b·|L(x) − L(y)| for all x, y ∈ S. Then a^n·H^n(L(S)) ≤ H^n(F(S)) ≤ b^n·H^n(L(S)) in [0, ∞], where H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P and the factors are ENNReal.ofReal(a^n) and ENNReal.ofReal(b^n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n P : ℕ) (F L : Euclid n → Euclid P) (S : Set (Euclid n)) (a b : ℝ), 0 < a → 0 ≤ b → (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, a * ‖L x - L y‖ ≤ ‖F x - F y‖ ∧ ‖F x - F y‖ ≤ b * ‖L x - L y‖) → ENNReal.ofReal (a ^ n) * μHE[n] (L '' S) ≤ μHE[n] (F '' S) ∧ μHE[n] (F '' S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (b ^ n) * μHE[n] (L '' S)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.8(i) (chapter-02.txt lines 270–296): H^m(f(A)) ≤ (Lip f)^m H^m(A) for Lipschitz f. As the printed proof notes, this holds even when A is not measurable. The lemma below is the Lipschitz step of step 3(b) in the supplied proof of the parent node, stated for an arbitrary reference map L in place of the linearization L₀ = DG(w₀).

Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm and H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P.

0. If S = ∅, then L(S) = F(S) = ∅ and all quantities are 0. Assume S ≠ ∅.

1. (Transfer maps.) For z ∈ L(S) choose λ(z) ∈ S with L(λ(z)) = z, and for z ∈ F(S) choose λ'(z) ∈ S with F(λ'(z)) = z (Function.invFunOn L S and Function.invFunOn F S, with invFunOn_mem and invFunOn_eq). Put φ := F∘λ and ψ := L∘λ'.
 (a) Let x ∈ S and x' := λ(Lx) ∈ S. Then Lx' = Lx, so |Fx' − Fx| ≤ b|Lx' − Lx| = 0. Hence φ(Lx) = Fx' = Fx, and φ(L(S)) = F(S).
 (b) Let x ∈ S and x'' := λ'(Fx) ∈ S. Then Fx'' = Fx, so a|Lx'' − Lx| ≤ |Fx'' − Fx| = 0. Since a > 0, Lx'' = Lx, i.e. ψ(Fx) = Lx. Hence ψ(F(S)) = L(S).

2. (Lipschitz constants.) Let x, y ∈ S. By 1(a), |φ(Lx) − φ(Ly)| = |Fx − Fy| ≤ b|Lx − Ly|, so φ is b-Lipschitz on L(S) (LipschitzOnWith with constant b.toNNReal, whose real value is b since b ≥ 0). By 1(b), |ψ(Fx) − ψ(Fy)| = |Lx − Ly| ≤ a^{−1}|Fx − Fy|; this is the hypothesis a|Lx − Ly| ≤ |Fx − Fy| divided by a > 0. So ψ is a^{−1}-Lipschitz on F(S).

3. (Lipschitz image bound.) If h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is K-Lipschitz on Y ⊆ ℝ^P, then H^n(h(Y)) ≤ K^n·H^n(Y) for arbitrary Y. This is Simon 1.8(i) for μH[n] (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), transported through μHE[n] = c·μH[n] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). In the import closure it is available as Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn.

4. (Upper bound.) By 1(a), 2 and 3, H^n(F(S)) = H^n(φ(L(S))) ≤ b^n·H^n(L(S)).

5. (Lower bound.) By 1(b), 2 and 3, H^n(L(S)) = H^n(ψ(F(S))) ≤ (a^{−1})^n·H^n(F(S)). Multiply by a^n. Since a^n·(a^{−1})^n = (a·a^{−1})^n = 1 (a > 0; ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_mul), this gives a^n·H^n(L(S)) ≤ H^n(F(S)).

For n = 0 all factors equal 1 and the same argument applies. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choosing preimages in S defines φ = F∘(L|_S)⁻¹ on L(S) and ψ = L∘(F|_S)⁻¹ on F(S). The two-sided hypothesis (with a > 0) makes them well defined, with φ(L(S)) = F(S) and ψ(F(S)) = L(S).
φ is b-Lipschitz on L(S) and ψ is a⁻¹-Lipschitz on F(S).
The Lipschitz image bound H^n(h(Y)) ≤ K^n H^n(Y) (Simon 1.8(i); SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), applied to φ and to ψ, gives the upper and the lower bound.

subproblem.statement: Let m, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{m+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, let D ⊆ ℝ^m be open and g : ℝ^m → ℝ^k a map that is C¹ on D. Put G(w) := ιw + ι'g(w) and J(w) := √det(DG(w)*∘DG(w)) with DG(w) = fderiv ℝ G w. Let t > 1 and w₀ ∈ D. Then there is r > 0 with B_r(w₀) ⊆ D (open ball) such that for every measurable B ⊆ B_r(w₀): H^m(G(B)) ≤ t·∫_B J dL^m and ∫_B J dL^m ≤ t·H^m(G(B)). Here H^m = μHE[m] on ℝ^{m+k}, L^m = volume on ℝ^m, ∫_B J dL^m is the lower Lebesgue integral of ENNReal.ofReal∘J over B, t enters as ENNReal.ofReal t, and the inequalities hold in [0, ∞].

Source. Supplied proof of the parent node, facts 1(ii)–(iii) and step 3(a)–(c). That proof makes explicit Simon's "approximation argument based on the linear case 3.1" for 3.2–3.3 (chapter-02.txt lines 760–776). The comparison constant c_ε of step 3(c) is replaced here by an arbitrary prescribed factor t > 1, which is what the globalization step needs.

Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm. For a continuous linear B : ℝ^m → ℝ^k write L_B := ι + ι'∘B. H^m = μHE[m] and L^m = volume.

1. (Derivative of G on D.) Let w ∈ D. Since D is open and g is C¹ on D, g is differentiable at w (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0, and D ∈ 𝓝 w). Hence G = ι + ι'∘g is differentiable at w with DG(w) = ι + ι'∘Dg(w) = L_{Dg(w)} (HasFDerivAt.add and the chain rule for the continuous linear map ι'; HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

2. (Lower bound for L_B.) For every B and h, |L_B h|² = |ιh|² + 2⟨ιh, ι'Bh⟩ + |ι'Bh|² = |h|² + |Bh|² ≥ |h|², because ι and ι' are isometric and their ranges are orthogonal (norm_add_sq_real). Hence |h| ≤ |L_B h|.

3. (The linearization at w₀.) Put B₀ := Dg(w₀), L₀ := DG(w₀) = L_{B₀} (step 1) and J₀ := J(w₀) = √det(L₀*∘L₀). By step 2, |h| ≤ |L₀h| for all h, so L₀ is injective. The sibling linear_area, applied to L₀ (n = m, P = m + k), gives det(L₀*∘L₀) > 0, hence J₀ > 0, and H^m(L₀(S)) = J₀·L^m(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^m.

4. (Choice of ε.) The function ε ↦ ((1 + ε)/(1 − ε))^{m+1} is continuous at ε = 0, where it equals 1 < t. Fix ε ∈ (0, 1) with q^{m+1} < t, where q := (1 + ε)/(1 − ε). Since 1 − ε ≤ 1 ≤ 1 + ε, we have 1 + ε ≤ q and 1/(1 − ε) ≤ q. Therefore
 (1 + ε)^m/(1 − ε) = (1 + ε)^m·(1/(1 − ε)) ≤ q^m·q = q^{m+1} ≤ t, and
 (1 + ε)/(1 − ε)^m = (1 + ε)·(1/(1 − ε))^m ≤ q·q^m = q^{m+1} ≤ t.   (∗)

5. (Choice of r.) Dg is continuous on D (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), hence at w₀. G is C¹ on D (ι is continuous linear and ι'∘g is C¹ on D), so DG is continuous on D, hence at w₀. The map T ↦ √det(T*∘T) is continuous: the adjoint is an isometric linear equivalence, composition is continuous, and ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det and Real.continuous_sqrt apply. So J is continuous at w₀. Choose r₁, r₂, r₃ > 0 such that:

 - |Dg(w) − B₀| < ε whenever |w − w₀| < r₂;

 Put r := min(r₁, r₂, r₃) > 0. Then B_r(w₀) ⊆ D. Fix a measurable B ⊆ B_r(w₀).

6. (Mean value inequality.) On the convex ball B_r(w₀) ⊆ D, the map w ↦ g(w) − B₀w is differentiable with derivative Dg(w) − B₀ (fderiv_fun_sub; a continuous linear map is its own derivative), and |Dg(w) − B₀| < ε there because r ≤ r₂. 9. (Integral of J over B.) For w ∈ B, |w − w₀| < r ≤ r₃, so (1 − ε)J₀ ≤ J(w) ≤ (1 + ε)J₀. Since B is measurable, monotonicity of the set integral and ∫_B c dL^m = c·L^m(B) (setLIntegral_mono', setLIntegral_const) give

subproblem.title: Area formula for measurable subsets of a C¹ graph: H^m(G(A)) = ∫_A J (supplied steps 1 and 4)
subproblem.statement: Let m, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{m+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, let D ⊆ ℝ^m be open and g : ℝ^m → ℝ^k a map that is C¹ on D. Put G(w) := ιw + ι'g(w) and J(w) := √det(DG(w)*∘DG(w)) with DG(w) = fderiv ℝ G w. Then for every measurable A ⊆ D, H^m(G(A)) = ∫_A J dL^m in [0, ∞]. Here H^m = μHE[m] on ℝ^{m+k}, L^m = volume on ℝ^m, and the right side is the lower Lebesgue integral of ENNReal.ofReal∘J over A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid m →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (m + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (m + k)) (g : Euclid m → Euclid k) (D A : Set (Euclid m)), (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → IsOpen D → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g D → MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ D → μHE[m] ((fun w => ι w + ι' (g w)) '' A) = ∫⁻ w in A, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (((fderiv ℝ (fun w => ι w + ι' (g w)) w).adjoint ∘L fderiv ℝ (fun w => ι w + ι' (g w)) w).det))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Supplied proof of the parent node, facts 1(i), 1(iv) and step 4 (countable decomposition and ε → 0), with c_ε replaced by an arbitrary factor t > 1 as provided by the sibling local_comparison.

Notation. ι* is the adjoint of ι, H^m = μHE[m] and L^m = volume. All integrals are lower integrals of ENNReal.ofReal∘J with respect to L^m.

1. (G is injective, and continuous on D.) First, ι*ι = id: ⟨v, ι*ιw⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιw⟩ = ⟨v, w⟩ for all v (LinearIsometry.inner_map_map, ext_inner_left). Second, ι*ι' = 0: ⟨v, ι*ι'u⟩ = ⟨ιv, ι'u⟩ = 0. Hence ι*(G(w)) = w for all w ∈ ℝ^m, and G is injective. G is continuous on D because ι and ι' are continuous and g is continuous on D (it is C¹ there).

2. (Two-sided bound for a fixed t > 1.) Fix t > 1. We show H^m(G(A)) ≤ t·∫_A J and ∫_A J ≤ t·H^m(G(A)). If A = ∅, all quantities are 0. Assume A ≠ ∅.
 (a) For each w₀ ∈ D, the sibling local_comparison (with this t) gives r(w₀) > 0 with B_{r(w₀)}(w₀) ⊆ D and both inequalities for every measurable B ⊆ B_{r(w₀)}(w₀).
 (b) ℝ^m is second countable, and each B_{r(w₀)}(w₀) is a neighbourhood of w₀. Hence there is a countable T ⊆ D with D ⊆ ⋃_{w₀∈T} B_{r(w₀)}(w₀) (TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin). T ≠ ∅, since A ≠ ∅ and A ⊆ D. Enumerate T = {e_0, e_1, e_2, …}, repetitions allowed (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range), and put B_j := B_{r(e_j)}(e_j).
 (c) Let A_j := A ∩ (B_j ∖ ⋃_{i<j} B_i), i.e. A ∩ disjointed B j. The A_j are measurable (MeasurableSet.disjointed) and pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed), and A_j ⊆ B_j (disjointed_subset). Also ⋃_j A_j = A ∩ ⋃_j B_j = A (iUnion_disjointed), since A ⊆ D ⊆ ⋃_j B_j.
 (d) G(A) = ⋃_j G(A_j). The sets G(A_j) are pairwise disjoint because G is injective (step 1). They are Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem: A_j is Borel, and G is continuous on A_j ⊆ D and injective (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; ℝ^m is Polish). By countable additivity of H^m (measure_iUnion) and of B ↦ ∫_B J (lintegral_iUnion, for disjoint measurable sets and any integrand):
 H^m(G(A)) = Σ_j H^m(G(A_j)) and ∫_A J = Σ_j ∫_{A_j} J.
 (e) By (a) with B = A_j ⊆ B_j: H^m(G(A_j)) ≤ t∫_{A_j} J and ∫_{A_j} J ≤ t·H^m(G(A_j)). Summing over j (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum, ENNReal.tsum_mul_left) gives H^m(G(A)) ≤ t∫_A J and ∫_A J ≤ t·H^m(G(A)).

3. (Letting t ↓ 1.) Let x, y ∈ [0, ∞] with x ≤ ofReal(t)·y for every real t > 1. As t → 1 from above, ofReal(t)·y → ofReal(1)·y = y: multiplication by a fixed y is continuous at a limit factor ≠ 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const, ENNReal.continuous_ofReal). Hence x ≤ y (ge_of_tendsto along 𝓝[>] 1). Apply this to both inequalities of step 2, which hold for every t > 1: H^m(G(A)) ≤ ∫_A J and ∫_A J ≤ H^m(G(A)). So H^m(G(A)) = ∫_A J (le_antisymm). ∎
proof_key_steps: ι*G = id (ι*ι = id, ι*ι' = 0), so G is injective; G is continuous on D.

For fixed t > 1, local_comparison gives balls around each point of D. Second countability gives a countable subcover, which is disjointified to a measurable partition A = ⊔ A_j with each A_j inside one ball.
G(A) = ⊔ G(A_j) with Borel pieces (Lusin–Souslin, injectivity). Summing the local inequalities gives H^m(G A) ≤ t∫_A J and ∫_A J ≤ t H^m(G A).
Letting t ↓ 1 in [0, ∞] gives equality.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the measurable-set area identity. Orthogonality supplies a continuous left inverse and injectivity. The countable cover and disjointification produce measurable pieces with disjoint Borel images, permitting both sums. Letting t decrease to 1 is valid in ENNReal even for infinite values because the limiting multiplier is nonzero. The sole child dependency is local_comparison.
